images.text:
Professional 1: Do you remember when companies had analog computers, mechanical adding machines and rotary calculators to perform their tasks in the office? Certainly, the IT world has changed substantially since those times, hasn't it?
Professional 2: That's true. Though archaic, those machines were the state-of-the-art for information technology purposes. I can say, however, that not all back times were better. With the advent of computers and computer networks, IT has now a great influence worldwide on many important aspects of a business. They're an influence on business strategy, organization culture, organization structure, and management processes. The way people work today and even IT has a huge influence in the workplace.

Professional 1: Definitely. In the future, with the new developments in IT, there won't be a project or business operation that can be conducted without the support of information technology. Individuals won't work in isolation any more even living or working in remote places if collaborative work is set. Subscribers to social networks will communicate far more easily in and out of work. Product design and development won't be made anymore without the aid of a design and simulation program connected to a network program to spread the information to different subsidiaries of a company around the world. In conclusion, info systems will bring lots of changes and benefits to the business world.

Professional 2: You're totally right, Bryan. The future seems to be very promising indeed. I'd like to say that at present information systems are hugely important for a business. That's why our profession is growing so fast. For example, companies won't be able to deploy a solid business strategy without information systems that help to collect large volumes of data. Then, its analysis followed by collaborative work that allows us to implement several initiatives along with monitoring and assessment tasks.

First Conditional With the Main Clause in Negative
The First Conditional is about a real condition with a possible consequence or result in the future.

The First Conditional is made of two clauses. The if clause expresses the condition, and the main clause expresses the possible future result or consequence. It doesn't matter which clause you use first, but in the case you begin with the if clause, use a comma to separate both clause.
Look at the examples:

• If we continue operating with this old-fashioned information technology, we won't be able to reach a competitive level soon.
  • We won't be able to reach a competitive level soon if we continue operating with this old-fashioned information technology.

Main Clause in Negative
The main clause, or also called the result clause, can be either positive or negative. The if clause can use any of the condition words as seen below:
  • Unless (if not)
  • So long as
  • As soon as (the moment)
  • Provided that (on the condition that / only if)
  • Whether (if)
  • After
  • Before
  • When

Grammar Structure
The grammatical structure for the first conditional is pretty straightforward.
If Clause
If + subject + verb (present simple) + complement

Main Clause
Subject + won't/may not/might not/cannot + complement
Example: If we replace timely some old computing equipment, the processes of the business won't collapse in the near future.
Individuals won't work in isolation any more even living or working in remote places if collaborative work is set.

Product design and development won't be made anymore unless the aid of a design and simulation program is connected to a network program to spread the information to different subsidiaries of a company around the world.
Before computers
Before computers, many of the tasks we do today were done with other electromechanical machines.
Do you remember when companies had analog computers, mechanical adding machines and rotary calculators to perform their tasks in the office?

Though limited by the potential for making calculations, for many years mechanical, and later on electromechanical machines, were used for this purpose. They, however, helped to reduce time in such calculations and also gave accuracy when performing tasks that usually fell into the field of bookkeeping and counting. To illustrate this idea, it is necessary to date back to the times of electromechanical adding machines or how about the manual rotary calculator. Not long ago, however, we can recall the use of mechanical typing machines and a rudimentary programmable calculator: the Olivetti Programma 101.

There were other useful machines before computers for handling large amounts of data such as the punched card data processing, which was used for a census in 1890. So when watching TV, you have probably seen those black & white programs in which very old computers were displayed with large tape holders spinning and processing the data contained in a magnet tape. The first computers used analog voltage levels instead of binary numbers, and the measurements taken by them were far from being accurate. By making comparisons of voltage levels, data was collected and therefore databases were created. It was necessary to take several measures to make sure it was correct.
